claims.text: The formation and persistence of a protective oxide above 900 °C in CrFeCoNiX alloys is governed by selective oxidation kinetics of the X element.
Al oxidizes more slowly than Mn or Si in the specified CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX forms a continuous and adherent Al2O3-based scale, potentially complemented by Cr2O3.
An Al2O3-based scale reduces thermal-expansion mismatch and diffusional stress.
Mn is selectively or preferentially oxidized in CrMnFeCoNi.
Mn oxidation in CrMnFeCoNi produces a non-protective oxide scale.
Mn-rich oxides grow rapidly, have high diffusivity and unfavorable mechanical properties, and consequently crack or spall under thermal stress.
Si-rich oxides grow rapidly, are discontinuous or poorly adherent, and tend to crack or spall.
Better lattice matching and lower thermal-expansion mismatch make the proposed Al2O3 scale more adherent and durable.
The relevant alloys are near-equiatomic CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solutions in either a single-phase or multiphase state.
The proposed comparison uses approximately 950 °C exposure in air or controlled oxygen partial pressure for an extended duration such as 100 hours.
Under identical oxidation conditions, the Al-containing alloy will have a slower-growing, more continuous and more adherent scale than the Mn- or Si-containing alloys.
The Al-containing scale will remain intact during prolonged high-temperature exposure, whereas the Mn- and Si-containing scales will crack or spall.
A CrFeCoNiX variant containing an inert or less-reactive X that does not contribute significantly to the protective scale can serve as the baseline.
The hypothesis is intended to apply only above 900 °C, in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres, for prolonged exposures and near-equiatomic compositions.
Microstructural features and small compositional deviations may influence oxide-formation kinetics.
Failure of the Al alloy to outperform the Mn and Si alloys in scale continuity, adherence and growth rate would falsify the hypothesis.
